document: Run the National Lottery mainly for the benefit of the NHS for at least 5 years, For the next five years we want two thirds of National Lottery proceeds to go to the NHS. The NHS benefits everyone in the UK. Small charities could still benefit from the remaining third. Art and theatre can gain income from other avenues. At the end of 5 years, these arrangements can be reviewed., The NHS is in crisis through mismanagement and under funding. The Government is short of funds. The National Lottery is an ideal way to get those funds. We believe more people would buy lottery tickets if the NHS was the main beneficiary, and be proud doing it.

Increase support for homeless people, Homelessness has always been a big issue in this country. I think the Government should provide additional funding to help the homeless. This could include more funding for accommodation, direct financial support and additional help to find work., I want the Government to take action as it is the Government's duty to protect us and make sure we are safe and have a roof over our heads. As an individual there is only so much you can do to support homeless people, and only the Government can take the action needed to support homeless people in the long term. We want to see the Government take immediate action to better support homeless people.

Make MPs who are absent from their constituency and Parliament subject to recall, A recall petition is opened if an MP is suspended from the Commons for ten sitting days, or certain convictions. However, there is no sanction for MPs who choose to be absent from constituency and Parliament while House sits. Constituencies should expect a minimum standard of service from their MP., The nature of the MP's role means that they may be required to work some distance from home, but there are long recesses when Parliament does not sit. There are nonetheless reports of MPs taking holidays or otherwise choosing to be absent when the House is sitting.
 
If MPs are absent from their constituency and Parliament for 10 sitting days, we believe they are failing to provide their constituency with the representation the taxpayer is paying for. In this situation a recall petition should be opened so the constituency can decide whether to recall them.

Fund free parking for all staff at NHS hospitals, All hospital workers should be able to park at their place of work for free, and not subjected to having to pay at a parking meter like visitors., Free parking for hospital workers should have no time restrictions so they do not have to worry if their shift overruns.

Hospital staff that we have celebrated during the pandemic for the vital role they played, and are now striking to boost their pay, should not have to pay to park their cars whilst they work. It is disgraceful they are not given free parking to avoid the indignity of a parking ticket at the end of their shift. It is no wonder there is an NHS staff retention problem when we overlook basic benefits for them such as this.

For GP’s and NHS Psychiatrists to Screen women aged 39 plus for Perimenopause, Create awareness that many women are being misdiagnosed with depression and anxiety symptoms without questioning their menstrual cycle and using a screening tool to indicate if this is peri menopause related symptoms., I am petitioning for this due to my own personal experience and recognise many other women will be at some point in their life in the same situation. This will help government not only save money and time as it will help keep women in the work place if perimenopause is detected early on but will prevent hospital admissions and referrals to mental health services if women are screened and identified early on as suffering with this. GP’s and key health professionals need a perimenopause screening tool.

Introduce fines for failure to attend NHS appointments and mandatory reminders, Each missed NHS hospital appointment costs the NHS around £160. A fine for failure to attend should help cut this. Non-attenders inflate waiting times considerably. I suggest £10 for a missed GP appointment, £50 for a hospital appointment and £150 if you miss an operation without good reason., A reminder letter should be sent 2 weeks before the appointment, followed up by a phone call to confirm attendance. A list of those who can come at short notice could be kept in case of cancellations.

Fund cervical cancer screening from the age of 18, I want the Government to provide funding so that all women can access cervical cancer screening from the age of 18., I believe this could make a difference to all women, by enabling early detection of cell changes that could turn into cancer.
 
I’ve had symptoms of cervical cancer for two years. This has been a difficult journey for me, and I am still in the process of my diagnoses. If screening had been available when I was 18, I believe this would have been a much easier process for me. I am creating this petition for young women in the same situation as me; I don’t want anyone else to experience what I’m going through.

Make tax returns for MPs public records for the duration of their appointment, Transparency clause for all MPs so that on their successful appointment, their personal and business tax information will be public record throughout the duration of their appointment and subject to Freedom of Information requests., We believe it is in the public interest for the financial affairs of MPs to be more transparent during the period of their appointment. In light of recent revelations, we want the public to have access to information about the financial affairs of MPs so they can better judge the interests and integrity of the people they have elected to represent them.

Require open public scrutiny of all MPs tax records, We believe becoming a Member of Parliament is an honour and privilege and people seeking this public office should be held to the highest standards of ethics and integrity. Requiring public scrutiny of all MPs personal tax affairs would give confidence to their electors., We think open and accountable Government starts at the level of the individual Member of Parliament. Open government is good government, for the people of the UK to trust their government the MPs must also trust the scrutiny of the people of the UK. We expect the highest standards of honesty and integrity in both the performance of their official duties and the arrangements of their private affairs. Both should bear the closest public scrutiny.

Petitions passing 1 million calling for a general election, should be honoured, Enact legislation such that if an e-petition calling for a general election gains more than 1 million signatures, then the Government must call a general election., Public opinion on the current Government is one the lowest for almost any incumbent government, yet the public are unable to force a general election.
 
If the country is to be run democratically, then the people should be listened to, especially if they want a general election.

Require separate NHS areas for people experiencing pregnancy complications/loss, We want the Government to protect people experiencing pregnancy complications and/or pregnancy loss from unnecessary distress by requiring the NHS to offer a separate space/waiting area for people experiencing this., Make it mandatory for NHS to offer this space at first contact. This could be done by using a code word at arrival for patient appointments, so NHS staff can easily recognise without having to check patient notes (which is often after the patient has already been placed in a general waiting area). Staff can then offer a separate space immediately meaning vulnerable patients are in a safe and comfortable space, free from upsetting triggers whilst waiting to be seen.

Stop road tax until the roads are safe from potholes and damaging our vehicles, Cancel road tax until you fix the unsafe roads we drive our roadworthy vehicles on that keeps damaging our vehicles, They get the money from road tax which is not being spent on our roads that you think our safe to drive on

Fund improved diagnosis in health care settings, We believe many hospitals are failing to provide a high enough standard of care to their patients when diagnosing them. Some patients are diagnosed too late or are mis-diagnosed and we believe that hospitals and care settings would be able to limit these errors with more funding and resources. , My mum had a fall in 2020 and was taken to hospital. Just 16 days later we were told they had found 3 brain lesions which were cancerous, with a life expectancy of weeks to a short few months, and placed in a care home. November 2022 an MRI scan showed she had brain damage in both frontal lobes and not cancer. Sadly mum passed away 3 days later. 2 years of steroids she shouldn’t have been on caused muscle weakness and she became bed bound, causing pressure on her heart until it stopped.

Invest to guarantee women’s access to breast screening – now and for the future, Screening saves lives from breast cancer. But since the pandemic started, it is estimated over 1 million women have missed out on screening in England, and thousands may be living with undiagnosed breast cancer as a result. The Government must urgently invest in breast screening to prevent deaths., Despite being one of the NHS’s biggest success stories, breast screening is at breaking point. Without investment, it may no longer be the powerful, cost-effective tool for early diagnosis it’s been for the past 35 years.

We need breast screening that is accessible to all eligible women and has enough staff and resources to offer the care women deserve, now and in decades to come.

More Government funding is needed to remove barriers to screening, support units, and modernise the programme.

Do not permit any Council Tax increase of more than 5% without a referendum, No local authority should be able to increase Council Tax by more than 5% without a referendum. The Government should instead renegotiate its settlements with local authorities in England to find a way to resolve the exceptional financial difficulties that many councils find themselves in., The public should not have to pay for a financial crisis which is not their fault through Council Tax increases above the 5% cap, unless these are approved through a public referendum.
 
Many people will be placed in dire financial circumstances during the cost of living crisis if their local authorities are allowed to raise Council Tax by more than 5%.

Make all WW2 service records public, WW2 service records are protected under the Data Protection Act and the MOD's own policies. This petition is asking for an exception to the Data Protection Act, and changes to MOD policy, so that all WW2 service records are published. We believe this would be in the public interest., Publishing these records could be a source of closure and healing for veterans, as well as their families. Having easy access to the records may help them to better understand their loved ones and the war they served in.
 
There are very few WW2 veterans left - being in their 90s and 100s. Publishing the records could answer many questions for certain individuals and might help to reunite lost comrades.
 
A final goodwill gesture to those who saved the nation and the planet, so that they may rest in peace.

Fund genomic analysis for child cancer patients to improve treatment, We want to see the Government provide funding to the NHS to make genomic analysis available to all cancer patients up to the age of 18., Every child diagnosed 0-18 with cancer should be able to receive genomic analysis, allowing scientists to look for genetic alterations that may be driving the cancer’s growth, so that drugs capable of targeting those alterations can be identified.
 
This information could be used by the consultant treating the child to help them make an informative specific treatment plan. This could help offer more treatment options and a better insight into research for the future.

Abolish the Dart Charge for cars and other light vehicles, Abolish the £2.50 charge (or £2 if you have an account) for cars and other light vehicles., In 1999 the government said the Dartford Crossing toll would be free to use by 2003, but backtracked in 2001. The cost of construction was paid off in 2002.
 
The Severn Crossing abolished tolls years ago, and the Dartford Crossing should be the same.
 
Especially during the current cost-of-living crisis, we believe the charge is unnecessary and for some families, extortionate.
 
The charge should remain in place for goods vehicles to help cover maintenance.

Extend qualified one-way cost shifting to Equality Act discrimination claims, Amend the civil procedure rules (44.13) to extend qualified one-way cost shifting arrangements to discrimination claims under the Equality Act (2010)., Disabled people like myself can find it extremely hard to sue big organisations for discrimination. When I did this I was taking a huge financial risk. And chose to settle out of court when I didn't really want to because of the financial risk. I believe that extending qualified one-way cost shifting from personal injury cases to discrimination cases will make it much easier to get affordable legal representation when individuals like myself want to take legal action against big organisations.

Require daily council tax discounts by councils that fail to maintain roads, Motorists have to keep our cars roadworthy and can be fined if they are not kept to the standard, I believe we should be holding local authorities to the same standard, that if a road is not adequately maintained, then they should be required to reduce council tax charges for each day until it is., Local authorities are allowed to charge us for driving through certain areas based on emissions. Whilst that is a different argument for another time, we believe that local authorities should be required to reduce council tax charges for each day, for each road that is not adequately maintained and car worthy.

This should be an impactful enough amount to ensure that the local authority actually takes accountability and makes the appropriate action within a reasonable time.

Give school staff powers to take enforcement action against illegal parking, Authorise school staff to take enforcement action against illegal parking, to help them better control traffic at pickup and drop-off and ensure a safer environment for children and families., Currently many school staff are left to manage parking difficulties at pickup and drop off, often facing abuse or being peace keeper between parent and resident disputes in more built up areas.
 
Giving them powers take enforcement action against illegal parking would mean they were better able to fulfil this role. This should also reduce the burden on full time wardens and provide an additional revenue stream to the local councils.

Require public referendums on 15-minute town and city policies, We want the Government to pass legislation requiring local, legally binding, referendums to approve 15-minute cities before such a policy can be implemented. Public referendums must be held on these policies., People need to be given the choice about whether or not they want these policies to be implemented in their areas. We believe it's far too important for the people not to be allowed to vote on these policies before they are implemented!
 
In the short term, we want local councils to be required to hold local, legally binding, referendums before they can implement a 15-minute city policy. We also want a legally binding national referendum on whether any local authority should be able to implement a 15-minute city policy.

Review access to IVF for people with a high BMI, Too many people have the basic right of starting a family stopped due to weight., I want the Government to review access to IVF for people with a high BMI, so that action can be taken to provide a better service and treatment for couples seeking fertility treatment that have a high BMI.
 
We need to stop fertility discrimination using weight and take a more individual approach.
 
Because it’s unfair people can be preventing from exercising a basic human right due to unfair weight criteria.

Extend regulation of health services to medical services at events, To extend regulation of health services to medical companies providing care at sport, entertainment and cultural events.
 
Currently medical companies providing these services are not regulated, which can contribute to variabilities in the standards of care given to patients in the event setting., Medical companies need to be held accountable by a regulatory that has powers to check staffing qualifications, equipment and areas of knowledge for the fields they work in to ensure they are providing the right care to patients.
 
Without regulation patients are being put at risk and event organisers have no idea who to trust.

Make it a specific criminal offence to leave a child under five unsupervised, We are calling on the Government to bring in a new law that prohibits those responsible for a child under the age of five to leave them unsupervised., We would like it to be a criminal offence to: "Leave a child aged under five alone without supervision, where the person responsible for the child's health and safety is unable to reasonably react to any circumstances that may expose said child to the risk of injury or death."

Partially privatise the NHS, Our NHS is now broken and no longer provides proper health care. GP surgeries, ambulance and hospital services are stretched to breaking point.  People are suffering and dying and we cannot claim to be cared for. We need to look at a German or French system partly funded by specialist insurance., Only parliament can address this issue. We need to introduce an insurance based funding perhaps along the lines of the German or possibly the French system where specialist insurance companies are used to fund care by employment deductions and reasonable charges for appointments and some routine services. If we don’t bring more guaranteed regular funding and take politics largely out of our health care we can no longer get the care we all need.

Fund HPV home tests as an alternative to cervical screening, Many people are put off having a Cervical Screening due to how invasive and embarrassing some might find them. A HPV tests for abnormal cervical cells and are proven to be a good alternative to a Cervical Screening and this can be done in the comfort of your own home by yourself with a simple swab., The NHS do not provide these tests as a standard alternative in all areas, but I believe it should be as it can save multiple lives. Younger people who are worried will be able to test themselves and it could overall save the NHS of money.
 
Provide funding to roll out HPV Home Test Kits from the NHS as an alternative to a Cervical Screening.
 
https://www.england.nhs.uk/2021/02/nhs-gives-women-hpv-home-testing-kits-to-cut-cancer-deaths/

Put Zebra crossing on Franche rd A442 by the entrance to White Wickets park, It is essential for a zebra crossing to be put close to white wickets park as families try and cross this busy road all the time. There has been an inquest into speeding down this road and this could help part of the problem as you tend to find most speeding within school run hours., School children and families are always trying to cross the busy road and with concern about speeding, it would help people cross safely. I have just had to help a child cross this busy road as no car stopped to allow them to cross. With people caught speeding down this road having a zebra crossing could help prevent an accident. You ask why? Well for the safety of children and their families!

Ban Gambling advertising nationwide on all media platforms, We believe gambling advertising is a predatory practice heavily targeting the young, the poor, and especially those in need of financial resources., Gambling ads can be seen and effect vulnerable groups and should be banned, even though gambling itself can remain legal for willing participants.
 
Gambling ads often suggest anyone can get rich, but the main beneficiaries of gambling are the gambling companies.
 
We believe gambling advertising brings no benefit to society; and that it is a malicious tool designed to divert money from those who need it the most, to those who need it the least.
 
Other nations such as Italy, Belgium and Singapore and United Arab Emirates have applied similar policies, and we want the UK to follow suit.

Require impact assessments and approval of MPs for all emergency legislation, Replace emergency procedures in the Public Health Act 1984 (including the section 45R, the urgency procedure that allows a single minister to implement emergency legislation), with revised legislation that requires an impact assessment and approval by MPs before legislation comes into effect., The Health Protection (Coronavirus, Restrictions) (England) Regulations 2020 was enacted without an impact assessment and parliamentary approval happened post implementation. There is increasing evidence that lockdowns & other non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) caused harm to large numbers of people.
 
Children's education was harmed, medical treatment delayed and people's health & fitness substantially reduced. Isolation caused mental health issues, especially for children, elderly & those living alone.

Path from Flitwick Road in Maulden to be able to safely walk to Redborne., I would like there to be a safe and easy-to-access path that connects Maulden to a Ampthill which is home to schools that our residents go to.  

There are two paths that connect them, but they are not accessible and safe enough (one is a footpath through a field, the other takes too long)., With this path, there would be less cars on the road, meaning less pollution, traffic, and noise; especially on weekdays with the school run.  

Kids would also be able to walk to school with their friends, and not have to rely on being dropped off by parents or pay for bus fares. 

Dog owners will be able to use this path to access the green areas around Abbey Lane, and people can walk to Flitwick easily to use their amenties, including the new Aldi that is under construction.

Provide funding for specialist community centres targeting homeless youths, We want the Government to provide funding for specialist community centres targeting homeless youths, with a particular focus in urban areas., Young people face many risks if they become homeless, including falling into prostitution or survival sex.
 
There is too little targeted provision for these young people and many are scared to go to shelters for adults. Increased funding could support the creation of new specialist community centres targeting homeless youth, and work to increase awareness of support for homeless youths.

Fund free sanitary products for homeless women, We want the Government to fund free sanitary products for menstruation free for homeless women. This means that women who are homeless should be given access to free products, distributed on streets and in homeless shelters., These items are not optional or luxury items. They are a necessity and women cannot live comfortably without them. There are many cases where women are stealing these items and providing them for free should reduce crime and the criminalisation of women.

To make minimum wage equal for all ages to end age discrimination for pay, I want the minimum wage to be made equal for all ages. The minimum wage is currently less for adults aged 18-22 years of age no matter what experience you have. This means workers aged under 23 can be paid less than older staff, even if they have more experience and qualifications., I would like the Government to re-consider the rates for minimum wage and make it fair. I believe employers should look at the experience and qualifications a person has rather than their age. It is not fair that you can get paid less due to your age. It is age discrimination.

All employers must have Automated External Defibrillators., Mandate in legislation, specifically First Aid Regulations 1981 to ensure all employers have at least 1 AED (Automated External Defibrillator) available on their site,  based on the employers first aid risk assessment., Heart and circulatory diseases cause a quarter of all deaths in the UK, that’s more than 160,000 deaths each year – an average of 460 deaths each day or one every three minutes in the UK.
In the UK there are as many as 100,000 hospital admissions each year due to heart attacks: that's one every five minutes.
More than 900,000 people in the UK are living with heart failure.
Strokes cause around 34,000 deaths in the UK each year and are the biggest cause of severe disability in the UK.
SAVELIVES

Provide funding for helplines for young people who are at risk of homelessness, In each part of the country there should be Government-funded helplines that can support younger people who may be at risk of becoming homeless., I want the Government to do this because too many young people are left stranded on the streets after being kicked out of home or running away. This can put the young person in danger, and we want the Government to make sure they have easy access to advice and support.
 
It is estimated that over 120,000 children and young people are homeless. Every year 100,000 children and young people go missing or run way from home and nearly 100 teenagers are made homeless each day in the UK as a result to alcohol abuse.

Change the decision to scrap cash payment meters for parking in towns & cities., We want them to keep cash parking meters in towns and cities across the UK., Lots of people across the country are fully against the decision to scrap cash parking meters. 

It's discrimination against older people or people who simply prefer cash. 

We do not wish to become a cashless society not matter what some may say. 

There is a vast amount of people in this country who are not tech savvy and they should not need to learn all about tech because they 'have to'

We petition the government to change their mind on this issue and stop any dissemination that may occur.

the government to give more funding to provide more homeless shelters., to open more homeless shelters and help younger homeless people., to get more homeless people off the streets and provide them with the basic human needs they need to survive. for example hot meals. 78% of homeless people sleep rough in Birmingham on the average. WE NEED CHANGE TO HAPPEN

Create a Legal Duty of Care to End Homelessness, We currently choose not to end homelessness, despite having the wealth to do it. We are all responsible for the failure, yet no one is adequately accountable. It is a legal duty to provide a free place for education. It should be legally required to offer shelter for all. It's a human right., This is not a party political issue and we believe should be backed by all elected representatives. There should be no question of "if" anything is done, but "how." We need the Government and local authorities to be placed in a position of responsibility and held to account for its delivery. It is a humanitarian issue and funds should be ringfenced specifically for this task. Instant solutions must be found or made. If we can build world-leading hospitals in 2 weeks for COVID, we can build homes. This should no longer be left to charities.

Fund free Diagnostic Assessments for Dyslexia for all Children aged 7-19, We believe the process for getting an assessment for dyslexia is unfair and favours high income families., Diagnostic assessments for dyslexia, should be free for children aged 7-19, in full-time education.
 
It can cost £600+ for an assessment. Many parents/carers can't afford this, and many schools will only help if child has a formal diagnosis.
 
Too few schools/LEAs will pay for the diagnostic assessment for dyslexia. Instead parents/careers have to pay.
 
Dyslexia is covered by the Equality Act 2010, yet without a formal dyslexia diagnosis many dyslexic children are not getting the help they need, such as extra tutor support and extra time in exams.
 
It can be extremely difficult to get an EHCP for dyslexic children without a formal diagnosis. This means a child can miss out on extra funding to help them learn.

Fund free sanitary and hygiene products for the homeless, Our aim is for the Government to provide funding to enable the supply of free sanitary and hygiene products (menstrual products, toothbrushes, toothpaste, hand soap) to the homeless people in our community., On average women have to spend £4,916 on menstrual products in their lifetime. These unfortunate homeless women and young adults are struggling every single month on something so many people take for granted. We believe that it would be beneficial for the Government to work with local authorities, local businesses and retailers to provide free sanitary and hygiene products to the homeless. This could be done by handing out vouchers at shelters and foodbanks that can be redeemed through businesses in the local area.

Repeal the Vagrancy Act (1824), Repeal the Vagrancy Act, which currently criminalises rough sleeping and begging., The Vagrancy Act of 1824 makes it a criminal offence to sleep or beg for money. At a time where the cost of living and homelessness are spiralling out of control, it’s time to start helping the most vulnerable in our society instead of punishing them.

Require paid parking operators offer multiple payment methods, Too many paid parking operators, including local authorities, are moving towards only accepting payment by app. This alienates people that can't or prefer not to use apps., What about people who can't use apps or don't want to because we are concerned about the use of our data. I should not be expected to download an app to pay for parking. Paid parking operators should be required to offer multiple payment methods, so no-one is unable to pay for parking because they can't or don't want to download an app.

Set time limits for funerals in England, I am asking for a law to be introduced setting a time limit on how long the deceased may be held without a funeral or being otherwise respectfully cremated or buried., Currently there is no law on how long a deceased person may be held by a funeral home, before a funeral must be held.
 
This can mean that funerals are not held for months after a person deceased. This is a particular issue when there are family disputes about holding a funeral.
 
We believe this is disrespectful to the deceased, who deserve to have their funeral. This can be extremely upsetting to friends and family of the deceased.

Create powers to increase sentences where a defendant refuses to attend court, Where a defendant is in custody but refuses to attend court, we want the courts to be given powers to increase any sentence applied., By refusing to attend court defendants are refusing to face the consequences of their actions. We believe this is an insult to the court and victims.
 
If a defendant refuses to attend court then judges should have the power to add a penalty term for non-appearance of up to 5 years dependant on the offence.

Do not cut investment in social care workforce , The Government had previously announced £500 million to improve recruitment, retention, progression, and staff wellbeing in social care. This has now been cut by 50% to £250 million. We believe this should be increased back to the £500 million originally announced., We believe the Government isn't taking a short, medium or long term view for social care.
 
About 400,000 people left their jobs in 2022, 1/4 of the workforce. If this isn't addressed frail and vulnerable people will go without the care they need.
 
There are 165,000 vacancies, a 52% increase on the previous year and the highest on record.
 
Care workers were paid an average hourly rate of £9.66 in the independent sector and £11.03 in the public sector.
 
Increased investment in workforce development is what is needed.

Introduce 'Deutschland-Ticket'-style monthly public transport ticket for £40-45, Work with transport operators and devolved administrations, and provide funding to introduce a monthly ticket for £40-45 for all local public transport, to make this more affordable and encourage people to use public transport than using car., Germany has recently introduced a €49 monthly ‘Deutschland-Ticket’ covering all local transport.
 
Introducing the same scheme here should encourage more people to use public transport, helping to reduce carbon emission, achieve Net Zero target and help reduce demand on fuel by reducing the number of vehicles on road. Having fewer vehicles on road would help to reduce traffic on road and could increase the average speed of buses. This should help to attract more car users to switch to public transport. Working with the devolved administrations to make it valid throughout UK on all local public transport should make it more attractive to people.

Stop Hawkinge /Folkestone being gridlocked., Implement procedures in place with KRS which stops surrounding areas being gridlocked and locals being prisoners in own homes., Local MP's do nothing. Locals unable to get to work, see sick relatives. get to hospitals if emergency.

Fund increased access to PARP inhibitors for cancer patients through the NHS, PARP inhibitors can be effective at treating certain cancers, yet they only recommended for use in the NHS in limited circumstances. We want the Government to provide funding to increase access to PARP inhibitors, which can save lives and improve quality of life., The Government is responsible for people's lives. It is also responsible for the UK's healthcare system. As the healthcare system is now able to administer a drug which can enable some cancer patients to live better lives (PARP inhibitors), with fewer and less severe side effects than chemotherapy, it is the Government's responsibility to ensure access to these for all who need it, whenever they need it, regardless of its cost.

I'd like guards or some sort of security on public transportation, To put security and patrols on public transportation, This can help reduce the amount of children missing the security can ask questions make the relevant calls if they see a young child travelling alone late at night this could reduce the time a child is missing and be returned home safely with no harm to them

Require taxis and private hire vehicles be licensed in the areas they operate, We want the Government to require taxi and private hire vehicle drivers to be licensed in all areas they operate in. The Deregulation Act 2015 has created loopholes that allow big companies to monopolise this trade, which has affected rates., Some councils are reducing the rates for taxi and private hire vehicle licences and making it easier to get a licence, eg. not needing to prove knowledge of local areas. This has resulted in a huge increase in licences being granted by some councils. People who are being banned from holding a licence with one council are going to other councils where they can easily obtain licences. The law has to change. Drivers should only be allowed to work in areas they have a licence for.

Reduce or remove corporation tax on Community Interest Companies, To please reduce or fully stop corporation tax on community interest company initiatives, which focus on social objectives, in a similar way to charities. This will enable CICs to help more people with the savings made, reducing pressure on the NHS and helping society., The savings will give CICs the extra funding they need to cover the massive costs they face. This could also help to reduce the pressure on public services like the NHS, police, ambulances and social services. Corporation taxes place extra strain on CICs and reduces the positive impact they can have in communities.

Stop car insurers considering age of driver when setting insurance policies, Car insurance should be based on the car model and any previous accidents the driver has been involved in, not in the driver's age or experience. Younger drivers should not face higher premiums, or requirements such as having a black box, because of their age., Many young drivers struggle to pay the high insurance premiums that insurers set for younger drivers. We believe this is unfair, and the Government should prevent it.

Require retesting of motorists found at fault in a road traffic collision, When people are at fault and have caused a road traffic collision, especially where this involves closures of roads and delay in business continuity, they should have to reattempt their test again, in line with current examination standards. This should be funded by the individual at fault., This should help protect people’s safety on the roads from dangerous drivers by ensuring people can meet current driving standards. This could also help to prevent chaos on the roads caused by accidents, as well as help to prevent people suffering due to accidents. It could also reduce strain on emergency services as they may not have to attend as many accidents.

Require all hospitals to have Frailty Guardians and Acute Frailty Units, We want the Government to require all hospitals to have Frailty Guardians, to advocate for and ensure the safety of all frail, elderly patients admitted via acute routes, and frailty units/wards, to address the healthcare inequity experienced by frail older people who live outside of large cities., The 2013 public inquiry at Mid Staffs NHS Trust recognised systemic failures in elderly care, today we are witnessing similar experiences within other NHS Trusts.
 
In 2023 some patients are still experiencing a lack of support with nutrition, hydration, hygiene, and toileting.
 
Missed care appears to be becoming acceptable ward culture, elderly patients are paying the price.
 
We believe the NHS is currently failing in its care of frail, elderly patients, urgent action is needed to resolve this issue.
Ban Smart Motorways, I believe that smart Motorways are now a death trap: the government needs to switch them off with immediate effect., They can cause deadly accidents.

Stop benefit sanctions for homeless benefit claimants, To understand rough sleepers may not be able to attend work searches due to not having a home, poor mental health or needing time to access homeless support. Homeless benefit claimants should not be subject to any actions., To give the rough sleepers time to work with a homeless organisation or their local authority, in order to settle them in some form of accommodation. Their needs should be assessed so they can fully renter society slowly, and feel safe and confident to find work.
 
When the benefits stop due to not attending work coach meetings this can prevent them from obtaining housing and set the process back. It’s hard enough for them sleeping rough

Ban all lane running on motorways, We want all motorways, including smart motorways, to have hard shoulders.
 
People have been killed because of all lane running on motorways, and we believe this should be banned, including on smart motorways., I am not aware of smart motorways being tried out with keeping the hard shoulders. I think smart motorways are an excellent idea if they retain the hard shoulder for safety reasons. We believe this would mean we can benefit from using technology to reduce congestion, without the safety risks of removing the hard shoulder.

Confirm that the next General Election will be no later than 28 January 2025, Under the Dissolution and Calling of Parliament Act, the next General Election must be scheduled to be held no later than 28/01/2025., We request that the Government confirms that the next election will be held by this date and the current Parliament will not exceed 5 years.
 
We believe it would not be democratic to extend the length of the current Parliament beyond 5 years.
 
There is currently nothing which prevents the law from being changed to allow the current Parliament to exceed 5 years. This could delay the date of the next General Election beyond what may ordinarily be considered acceptable to the majority of the public. We want the Government to confirm that this will not happen.

Create a fund to provide enhanced sick pay for workers on long-term sick leave, We want the Government to create a fund to enable employers to pay enhanced sick pay to workers who are on long-term sick leave (for example, 6 months at full pay, and 3 months at half pay). This would be especially helpful for workers suffering from serious conditions like a stroke or cancer.

, I am recovering from a stroke and work for a private company. While I'm off sick I'm only getting SSP.

I want employees to be able to access a Government fund so they can pay enhanced sick pay to employees who are on long-term sick leave, when they think this is appropriate. Employers should be able to decide how a worker's sick pay should be enhanced, and apply for money to pay for this from the Government fund.

The Government supported companies to pay staff who were furloughed during the covid-19 pandemic, so why not put something similar in place for workers who are on long-term sick leave, especially where this is for a serious condition like a stroke or cancer.

Provide public 'care of addresses' for homeless people, We want the Government to make public 'care of addresses' - for example at Jobcentre Plus offices - for homeless people, who do not have their own address and might not have anywhere they can use as a 'care of address', to ensure they can receive mail., To allow people to more easily access healthcare, food, shelter, and warmth, by being in contact with GPs and the DWP. Without this people can starve, and even die, on the street.

Lower the recommended mammogram age in the UK to 30., I want the Government and Parliment to recognise that the recommended age for a mammogram in the UK shouldn't be 51. It should be much lower, to protect the younger generation from Breast Cancer, so we can save younger peoples lives., It is so much more common in younger people than I think is recognised by the Government. The 25-30 year old age bracket has so many cases of Breast Cancer, the recommended age should be lowered to protect people. You cannot just rely on feeling for lumps as sometimes you cannot feel them. Lowering the age would save lives and allow for a much higher survival rate.

Fund bowel cancer screening from the age of 40, The NHS is expanding its bowel cancer screening programme to people aged 50 and over. We want the Government to fund this to start at 40. Too many people under 50 are being given terminal cancer diagnoses. If screening was offered earlier more cases could be caught earlier, saving more people., Too many clinicians don't test for cancer in people under the age of screening.
 
I personally have been ill for 4 years but was only diagnosed in December 2022, having previously been advised I was too young to have bowel cancer. If I had been tested earlier by diagnosis would likely have been far better, and the cost of my treatment lower.
 
Early screening should help identify cases earlier, and could save money overall.

Make legal aid available for disabled and vulnerable adults in private law cases, Make legal aid available for disabled and vulnerable adults with learning difficulties and for those aged under 18 years in private law cases. Having legal representation gives them a voice to correctly apply the law in support of their case fighting for family justice and their children., Vulnerable adults can struggle interpreting information or decisions that are made during law cases. We believe many families experience discrimination and bias in private law cases. It’s extremely difficult for vulnerable adults to self-represent as litigants and to learn the appropriate regulations/principles, including the legal way of writing, to successfully argue their case. Losing a legal case can have a negative impact on the mental health of vulnerable adults and their families.

Make SSP from first day of sickness and in line with National Living Wage, As it stands SSP is given if employees are sick for 4 or more days in a row, including your non-working days, and is paid at £109.40 a week.

Allow employees SSP from the first day of sickness and make payments in line with the National Living Wage for an employee's contracted hours., As it stands many people struggle to live on the current rate of £109.40 a week, and we believe this is not sustainable. People already facing a tough time are facing further uncertainty when they fall sick through no fault of their own. It is further exacerbated by the cost of living crisis where costs have risen exponentially. SSP has not risen adequately and needs to be linked to the National Living Wage, and paid from the first day of sickness.

To stop viability studies being used as a means to not meet social housing needs, we are infuriated at this method being constantly used to get out of social housing obligations but unfortunately with these big companies, they have the financial means to keep protesting their case and essentially knowing they will get their end goal using this approach., We are in the midst of a housing crisis across the UK and if we could stop these lathe organisations using this technique to get out of their social housing obligations, there would be more social/affordable housing for local people. Massively helping to relieve the UK housing crisis facing many low income families.

Improve detection of Breast Cancer via mandatory biopsies during Ultrasound scan, Mandatory biopsy during breast ultrasounds scans especially if a woman or man states they feel a lump on their breast. Biopsies are crucial to definitively diagnosing cancer. This can prevent invasive surgeries mastectomy), physical, mental trauma and the spread of cancer. It gives more options., Tony Blair executed the change of rule for all breast lump cases to be seen under the 2 weeks rule pathway however we need an increased screening of breast via biopsy to save women & men breasts. Let’s remember the Covid slogan Catch it, Bin it, Kill it ! We couldn’t see Covid but we felt the symptoms didn’t we? That is the same with Breast Cancer you can’t see it but symptoms show up so let’s Catch it, Kill it and Scoop it out by having upfront biopsies whilst having an ultrasound!

Stop individuals in non-fault accidents being charged more for car insurance, I would like the Government to ban insurers from taking into account non-fault accidents in car insurance prices/policies. , If a driver is not at fault, why should their insurance prices rise? People continue to be penalised for non-fault car accidents. 
 
This is obvious when renewing car insurance; if the claim is unsettled, then people may have to put that they are at fault, despite evidence they are not. This usually results in increased insurance charges. 
 
Car insurance overall can increase by 50% if you've been in an accident. This is not right or fair if the accident is not your fault. Why should the innocent person be charged because of someone else's carelessness?

Introduce mandatory driving assessments for 70 year olds and over, Pass a law that requires anyone with a driving licence who is 70 years old or older to take a driving assessment in order to continue to be able to drive. Their ability to drive safely, their spatial awareness and their reaction times to break if needed to stop in an emergency., As a car park attendant, I witness many older people driving in a dangerous manner, including driving into curbs and parked cars.
 
A mandatory driving assessment for driving licence holders aged 70 and over would ensure that older drivers are still safe to drive.

Require full sick pay for staff with long-term health issues, such as cancer
, Employers should be required to pay employees their full salary, including any additional payments that they have been getting for at least 3 months, if they need time off for a long-term health condition, such as cancer. This would allow them to receive treatment and recover without losing income., I am now experiencing how it is for a cancer patient to feel when they are recovering from cancer surgery and going on to have treatment. It is already a very difficult time to go through, and the stress of money worries should not be at the forefront of people's minds at this time. By having this requirement in place it gives every employee a little peace of mind to know that they will receive full pay while they receiving treatment or in recovery.

Reform laws barring people with no vision in one eye from getting an HGV licence, I want the Government to reform the legislation that bars people with no vision in one eye from being able to be licensed to drive HGVs, and introduce new rules that allow a licence to be granted if a driver can meet the same visual acuity and visual field standards as binocular drivers., I took a field of vision test at the opticians and received a score of 96% but as I'm blind in one eye I cannot get a licence to drive an HGV.
 
I want this to be reformed so that more people are able to become HGV drivers, which could help address the shortage of HGV drivers.

Ban public servants who breached COVID rules from all public service, We want the Government to ban any public servant, who has been found to have broken COVID rules, from holding public office or a position in the public sector. We want this ban to last for life and we want this ban to include MPs, civil servants and everyone employed through the public purse., We believe that confidence between the public and those in public office and the public sector has been damaged and that this ban would help to restore confidence, trust and integrity in those who hold public office or work on behalf of the public. It would help to show credibility and openness in our institutions and would respect the people of this country.
 
We think this ban would also help to ensure that, in any future national crisis, those working in public office or the public sector will follow the government’s rules, rather than dismiss them.

Introduce paid leave for employees to attend routine breast screening, Enable employees to receive paid leave to attend routine breast screening. At the moment there is no legislation for leave entitlement to attend these vital screening appointments. As more women are working for longer, it does affect the age group 50-70 year olds that are eligible for screenings., My breast cancer was detected from a routine breast screening appointment. I had no symptoms, yet had an invasive tumour. If people had a legal right to paid leave to attend these appointments, they are more likely to take up the offer of a screening. This could also help cut down on missed appointments. I'm campaigning for this to become a right and the time off be paid. Employees shouldn't be penalised for attending routine breast screening or indeed denied the time off to attend.

Review school exclusion policies and practices in academies, We are calling on the Government to appoint an independent panel to review school exclusion policies and practices in academies across the country. , This review should look at:  
 
- Existing practices around exclusion, and alternatives to these
- Rates of exclusion, including by ethnicity
- The role of Governors and headteachers in decision-making about exclusions.

Fund cervical cancer screening from age 16, and encourage take-up of HPV vaccine, Cervical cancer screening is currently available to those aged over 25, but I would like it to be available from the age of 16, as this is the age of consent for sex. This would provide support for all young women., Around 3,000 women are diagnosed with cervical cancer every year in the UK. The Government must also do more to increase take-up and encourage women who are eligible for a cervical smear test to attend their appointments. Ministers must also ensure that preventative measures, such as the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination for girls in secondary schools, are taken up as fully as possible.

Make the resale of event tickets for more than face value illegal, We want the Government to clamp down on ticket scalping. Too many people buy tickets only to sell them for double or triple the price, meaning- some fans miss out because they can't afford extortionate resale prices. Resale for more than face value should be banned, with penalties for offenders.,

Create a zebra crossing outside Lymington Infant & Junior school on Avenue Road, We request that a zebra crossing be placed outside the Lymington Junior and Infant school to slow traffic and help families cross the road safely., Avenue road is a busy fast moving road, with the fire station, town hall, police station and car parks adjacent to it. It’s also the main route around the town so traffic is steady and main lorries trucks are sent along it. For the safety of families and children crossing in and out of school hours we believe a zebra crossing would reduce the danger of a collision happening, keeping our children safe  - Pennington and Brockenhurst school both have zebra crossings.

Require rear facing car seats for children under 18kg, 105cm tall or 4 years, To ensure all infants involved in RTCs have the best chance of survival. Current law allows parents with lack of knowledge to put their infants in potential danger without even knowing. Although guidance is there, many infants are being put into forward facing seats as this isn't against the law., A rear facing seat will absorb most of the collision forces and supports the head; neck and spine. The seat keeps the spine aligned and limits damaging movement. When children ride forward facing, their heads - which for toddlers are disproportionately large and heavy are thrown forward. This can result in spine and head injuries such as fracture of the cervical vertebrae and internal decapitation. Organisations such as the NHS and Good Egg are already recommending rear facing car seats for longer.

Give patients a right to be seen by an NHS GP or dentist within three days , We want the Government to require GPs and NHS dentists to see patients within three days. , Since the pandemic many GP surgeries are difficult to contact and are not providing appointments in a timely manner. For many it is very difficult to find an NHS dentist. UK citizens contribute to the NHS through national insurance but the GP and NHS dentist system is failing the public.

We want the Government to impose a statutory duty to provide appointments within three days, which we believe is reasonable.

Do not allow the driving of SUVs on a standard driving licence, SUVs are unnecessarily dangerous to pedestrians and cyclists. Their size, weight and bonnet design can result in death or serious injury that would not be caused by a similar collision in a car. People should not be able to drive an SUV on a standard driving licence., We believe large heavy vehicles with high square bonnets are too dangerous to be a standard vehicle type, that can be driven using a standard driving licence.
 
We want the Government to revise the licence categories so SUV is a separate class, with its own licence.

Make hair colour a protected characteristic covered by hate crime legislation, We want hair colour to be made a protected characteristic to protect people with red or ginger hair from discrimination. Hate crime laws should also be extended to cover offences motivated by hostility or prejudice based on a person's hair colour., We believe current legislation does not adequately protect people with red or ginger hair, despite it being estimated that around 4% of people in the UK have hair this colour.
 
Too often people with ginger or red hair face prejudice, stereotyping and dehumanization.
 
For example, in response to an FOI North Yorkshire police disclosed that the words 'ginger', 'red hair' and 'redhead' appeared in crime reports 57 times from January 1 2021 to November 15, 2021.
 
There have been cases of hate crimes against redheads in the UK including stabbings, sexual harassment, groups attacks and targeting and abuse.

Require MPs to attend Parliament at least 8 times per year, There is currently no minimum requirement for the number of times an MP must attend Parliament over the course of a year. , We think that MPs must be held accountable if they do not attend regularly, especially when they are paid so handsomely.

Make MPs who are absent from their constituency and Parliament subject to recall, A recall petition is opened if an MP is suspended from the Commons for ten sitting days, or certain convictions. However, there is no sanction for MPs who choose to be absent from constituency and Parliament while House sits. Constituencies should expect a minimum standard of service from their MP., There are reports of MPs taking holidays or otherwise choosing to be absent when the House is sitting. 
If MPs are absent from their constituency and Parliament for 10 sitting days, we believe they are failing to provide their constituency with the representation the taxpayer is paying for. In this situation a recall petition should be opened so the constituency can decide whether to recall them.

Require private hire operators share fare breakdown with drivers, We want the Government to create a legal requirement for private hire operators to share the fare breakdown to drivers, with clear details of the service fee charged for a ride.,

Ensure fans are not forced in to buying top tier tickets to events., Prevent sites like Ticketmaster and AXS from holding back more affordable tickets in the favour of pushing VIP/More expensive tickets in general sales. They are taking advantage of people desperate to see shows who cannot necessarily afford the higher prices., Fans desperate for tickets have grabbed tickets at huge prices in panic at selling out in minutes. It appeared these shows had been sold out, but over the days after the initial general sale, Ticketmaster and AXS have made more affordable tickets available. There are no reasons these tickets should be available now except for the fact TM and AXS held back tickets to push VIP sales. People who spent between £200 and £600 on VIP packages are now left with worse seating than those paying ~£89.

Review local authorities statutory powers around residents parking charges., Local authorities seem to use car parking and especially residents/buisness car parking as a cash cow, they inveribly have '1 size fits' all policies which don't fit all scenarios and generally local authorities seem very draconian and not fair to those who live where they are being charged., The government need to introduce rules and regulations which councils need to work within as residents and business owners/workers are being continually punished by complex parking permit rules seemingly there only to be a cash cow to local authorities.

We are in a cost of living crisis yet parking permits continue to rise, some authorities have introduced 'digital permits' with the nuiances and cost not deemingly democratically voted on by local residents.

Fund routine breast cancer screening from the age of 30, The infrastructure is already in place. Women have regular mammograms through the NHS from age 50. We want this to be accessible to women younger than this and should be available from age 30., There has been a steady rise in the number of women who are diagnosed with breast cancer after age 30, often after having children. Younger women are often diagnosed with a later stage due to lack of screening and although self-exams are promoted, gland cysts are common in younger women who may ignore lumps due to their frequent occurrence. Therefore, we believe a more comprehensive check (ie. a mammogram) should be more widely available. Screening should mean earlier diagnosis and treatment and a more successful outcome.

Create a central management scheme for parking permits, Local authorities parking policies around all permits are overly complicated and overpriced. There needs to be more centralised, consistent and fair permit schemes which are easier to understand and adhere to. , Instigate policies and controls around what local authorities can do with regards to permits, especially cost of permits. Currently, we think that local authorities take advantage of being able to charge for parking permits.  At this very moment there is a cost of living crisis but permit prices are going up and it's complicated when it comes to workers needing to park for work at a business address.

Fund routine prostate cancer screening tests for all men over 40, Too many men find out they have prostate cancer too late. A simple PSA blood test can help identify prostate cancer, and we want the Government to provide funding to make this available to all men over 40, in the same way cervical screenings are available to women over 25., Funding routine screening for prostate cancer should help identify cases of prostate cancer earlier, enabling more effective treatment, and hopefully saving lives.

Provide parking badges for drivers with a child aged 0-5 in the car, Create a parking badge like the Blue Badge for disabled people for parking spaces designated for drivers with children aged 0-5. When a child is born a driver should get a badge which will be in date for 5 years., Most shopping places, car parks etc only have extremely limited parking for adults with small babies/children. Many people use these spaces even if they do not have a young child with them. This means people with small children have to park in less suitable spaces and can experience difficulties getting their children, pushchairs, bags, and shopping in and out of their car. Some car parks threaten fines but in my experience nothing is done about it. Having a child parking badge scheme would make it easier to identify and take enforcement action against people using these spaces improperly.

Require regular psychological screening of healthcare staff working with babies, We want healthcare staff - such as nurses and doctors - who are in contact with babies to be required to undergo regular psychological testing, in order to assess whether they are fit and safe to work with babies., Due to recent tragic events, we believe the Government must do more to ensure that people responsible for the healthcare of babies are fit and safe to work with babies, and have their best interests at heart.

Stop the DVLA divulging driver information to car parking companies, We want the Government to stop the DLVA from disclosing driver information to private car parking companies. Many of these companies are extremely aggressive in pursuing drivers, and the Government should not be sharing private information with these companies.,

Review the accessibility of Jobcentre appointments., A review is needed to ensure job centre appointments are accessible, including arrangements for Universal Credit and other benefit claimants can have telephone or video appointments where it is impractical for them to attend the Jobcentre., The review should particularly focus on the accessibility of Jobcentre appointments for people who struggle with sensory issues and anxiety.

Fund more research into childhood cancer and support for families, Childhood cancer research and support receives only a fraction of the funding that adult cancer receives, however can in some ways be more devastating for the patient and their family., Brain tumours kill more children than any other cancer, but can often go undetected or be misdiagnosed. Malignant brain tumours can be aggressive and can kill without being detected. The treatment can be harsh and so better funding for research into childhood cancers and support for childhood cancer patients (both with brain tumours and all other varieties of cancer), and their families, could greatly benefit these children and those around them.

Fund a walk-in mental health hub in every GP surgery and hospital, The Government should fund a mental health hub in every GP surgery and hospital, where no appointment is needed. For a person who is feeling suicidal, an appointment could be too late in saving them., Too many people die due to mental health issues and suicide. Currently the only options for help are to wait for a GP appointment or specialist referral or to call a helpline or go to A&E. All of these things require time, which for someone struggling could be too late in helping them. Having mental health hubs where no appointment is required to speak to someone, I genuinely believe could help so many people struggling.

Bring back the old system of GP appointments- the new system is not working!, If it’s not broken don’t fix it. Under the new system, people can’t get a GP appointment leading to more going to hospital or even deaths. When my Dad was a GP he made 15 appointments per clinic. You took a numbered paddle. You were seen in numerical order. Patients loved it- they got seen!, The authorities insisted he moved to appointments but he kept 5 slots available per clinic for emergencies. Government targets were emergency patients to be seen in 3 days. My Dad saw them same day! People with a long-term condition were seen every 3 months, keeping the condition under control minimizing hospital referrals. My Dad also had innumerable nurse led specialist clinics further keeping conditions under control. I am a former training GP and Joe Public wants this system back.

Fund routine breast cancer screening from the age of 25, Women under 50 should be able to access routine breast cancer screenings. Further tests can then be arranged as necessary, so that breast cancer is identified as early as possible, to maximise the chance of successful treatment and survival., I am 33 and I have been diagnosed with grade 3 invasive triple negative breast cancer. The first I heard of early screening options was in the cancer clinic waiting room on my diagnosis. I believe this is utterly unacceptable. 
 
Just because young women have denser breast tissue and are at a lower risk does NOT mean they should not be getting screened, to enable an early diagnosis, and better prognosis and chance of survival.

Require enclosure of bridges over motorways
 
, Protect the public and our professional drivers. The risk to life due to dangerous incidents involving bridges over motorways is unacceptable. Require the enclosure of all bridges over motorways to prevent people and objects falling and causing injury and loss of life to others., Motorists need to by protected and safe on our motorways and should not be victims of the actions of others whilst going about their daily lives, or livelihood. There are too many instances of objects being thrown from motorway bridges or people falling to their deaths and putting others lives at risk whilst moving in high speed traffic on the motorway with little time to react or defend themselves. The risk could be reduced by requiring these bridges be enclosed.

Make Universal Credit standard allowance the same for under and over 25
, We want the Government to increase the Universal Credit standard allowance for under 25s to equal that for people aged 25 and over. Many under 25s on Universal Credit struggle on the lower rate, which is £75 less than people aged 25 or over receive. This should be the same for all ages.
,

Make noise nuisance a criminal offence so police can take action, The Government should make noise nuisance after 10pm a criminal offence so that police can immediately respond to it. The police must warn them immediately, record their name and address, and there should be fines for repeat offences. 
 
, Offenders should also have to complete a community education scheme.

Noise nuisance can leave people including babies, elderly people and people who are unwell to suffer from anxiety and sleep deprivation. This can lead to people getting sick which can put more pressure on the NHS and Government welfare. Sleep deprivation can be very serious.

Address the delays in getting appointments for Driving Tests
, The government should ensure that the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) is funded and run efficiently in order to clear backlogs, ensure that driving test examiners are conducting a minimum of 6 tests per day and that there are enough examiners, and ban the resale of the practical tests., In order to gain a test appointment people often have to wait for months (sometimes a year). In some instances, the appointments are rescheduled by DVSA at less than one week's notice. Some people are unable to get to the university or work due to the lack of a driving license and the inability to get one, which I believe is due to the inefficiencies of DVSA.

Fund the reopening of the three state-of-the-art Rutherford Cancer Centres, Three state-of-the-art cancer centres lie empty in Newport, Reading and Northumberland - a concerted Government effort and funding would get these centres back open and potentially help 20,000 cancer patients every year., With record cancer waits, there is no time to waste.
 
Following financial difficulties during the pandemic, the network closed in June 2022.
 
I'm calling on the Government to step in with the funding and leadership needed.  Allowing thousands of UK cancer patients access to some of the most advanced diagnostic/treatment technology.
 
This is the worst cancer crisis of my lifetime. Reopening these centres could save countless lives.

Require police to attend every retail shop theft , The Government should require the police to attend every reported shop theft. Retailers feel unprotected and there has been a massive growth in offences. , In 2014, shop theft of goods below £200 was made a summary offence. 
 
I am a retailer based in Cambridge. I have been campaigning on this subject for many years. I believe that the crime of shop theft has become regarded by the public as a lesser form of crime. Recently various factors have conspired to see a large growth in the number of incidents. If this situation is allowed to continue and to escalate I believe it will become the norm and be impossible tide to turn back. The government must act now before it is too late.

Abolish the Blackwall Tunnel Toll, No Blackwall Tunnel toll., Blackwall tunnel is vital crossing to the east of London and is over due for a new connection but with all the tax you take you give noting in return, you want us to pay to cross at blackwall to pay for a new crossing at Thamesmead; which was planned years ago and already cost us £125 million until boris cancelled it and we lost that investment.
Yes build us a bridge at Thamesmead but why the poorer end of London will have to suffer extra costs at Blackwall Tunnel is a Joke.

The rich west part of London has many crossings and pays nothing for them.
Dartford Bridge has also gone up to £2 which we were told would be free once paid for.

No toll at Blackwall tunnel!
Stop punishing the workers.

Mandate all universities to provide holiday accommodation for estranged students, University students who lack family support can face homelessness during the holiday period, when university halls of residence expect students to “return home” to their families. For these students, the halls are their only home. Thus, holiday accommodation should be provided to estranged students., An estranged person is someone who has had no parental contact for at least 12 months, where this is unlikely to change.

Higher education is not accessible to those without family support if it is to cause them repeated homelessness. There exist some universities and independent non-profits which offer year-round accommodation to a small proportion of the care-experienced and estranged student population. However, this is not enough and this needs to be mandated on a national level.

Change school starting time to 10am, We think that schools should start from around 10am, because starting school at 8am is far too early.
 
School starting at 10am and ending at 4-5 is quite fair and reasonable because it will still allow students to still get their 6-7 hours of education needed.,

Any cancellation of HS2 (North) must be subject to Due Process, We ask Parliament: To ensure that any cancellation of HS2 North is subject to Due Process, and

We ask the High Court: To consider an Injunction against any disposal of HS2 North/its Assets by Gov't until said Due Process is followed, on the Assent of the Signatories to this Petition., HS2 North has received significant public funding for study, survey and design, and the section between Birmingham and Crewe has obtained Royal Assent. Cancelling HS2 North renders this investment lost, and such waste of public funds cannot be allowed to happen without appropriate scrutiny.

Any disposal of HS2 North & its Assets must first be subject to Due Process - Not rapidly sold-off by an (outgoing) Gov't for its own gain - And only furthered if this stands in the wider public interest.

Create a statutory Delay Repay scheme for all public transport, Enforce legislation for all public transport providers, such as public buses to have a delay repay and compensation scheme, similar to those for train companies, in order to compensate customers for any major delays due to the fault of the provider., There are many instances where buses simply don't ran, meaning a once-every-10-minute route can end up running only once per half an hour, causing major inconvenience such as missing connections onto other transport (despite leaving a long waiting gap), and missing appointments. We believe in situations like this passengers should be entitled to compensation.

Increase Universal Credit for families with disabled children, We urge the Government to increase Universal Credit for families with disabled children, to ensure they have the money they need to care for their children properly., The average London household pays £1,480 a month in rent, or £341 a week. Trying to pay for rent and care for a disabled child can be a struggle and we believe the Government's helping hand is not enough.
 
Families with a disabled child receive an extra £146.31 of Universal Credit a month, and families with a severely disabled child receive an extra £456.89 a month. Considering the needs of children with disabilities, including dietary requirements, energy bills increasing due to medical equipment and parking fees for hospital appointments, we believe this is not enough.

Ban recording using smart glasses without the knowledge of people being recorded, It is fairly easy to see when someone is recording with a smartphone given how they hold it. I don't think this is the case with smart glasses. This is sometimes only made evident by a light on the glasses, which cannot always be seen, and not all smart glasses have. , Whilst recording and sharing of personal data by smart glasses is covered by the Data Protection Act 2018, I think that new legislation should be introduced which specifically relates to preventing misuse of smart glasses, to prevent people from recording others without their knowledge.

Include details of significant case law on legislation.gov.uk, We want the Government to include significant case law relating to legislation on legislation.gov.uk., So, for instance, if I wanted to find relevant case law to s14(2) of the Sale of Goods Act 1979, it would be easily accessible from the legislation.gov.uk page for this legislation.
 
The law of England and Wales is created in case law as well as in statutory legislation. An understanding of legislation can be of limited help if one doesn't have access to precedent through which to interpret it. Therefore, keeping a record of this nation's legislation without also keeping a similar archive of important cases that have shaped said legislation, means that those with less legal experience may only be looking at half of the law. A corresponding case archive would help those without legal knowledge.

Create a fund for the provision of local radio services, We would like the Government to create a fund that radio operators can bid for to provide local radio services for communities. , I belong to a Facebook group where many are appalled at the recent cuts to local radio services. We believe that local radio services offer a very different listening experience to that of national radio. It has a local emphasis and, for so many (particularly those on their own), it provides company because listeners can contact the stations to take part in various features and the listeners can almost build a 'relationship/friendship' with the Presenters!

Create a grant for Universal Credit claimants to learn to drive, Introduce a grant specifically for people who are on Universal Credit to enable them to learn to drive and get a driver's licence., In the past year I have had five phone calls from companies wanting to hire me or knowing a company that would want to hire me but due to my location in relation to them it would either take far too long (over an hour) or be near impossible to get to the office by using public transport. Due to the amount of money I receive from Universal Credit I have not been able to learn to drive or get a licence, due to how much they cost.

Allow civilians a vote of no confidence in the government or a minister, Change the law so that civilians can initiate and participate in a vote of no confidence in the administration or against a specific minister. If the vote is successful, this would trigger a general election or the replacement of a minister., We need to be able to trust and have faith in our leaders and spokespeople in parliament. We believe this would help stop ministers and administrations breaking promises made during elections!

Require impact assessments and approval of MPs for all emergency legislation, Replace emergency procedures in the Public Health Act 1984 (including the section 45R, the urgency procedure that allows a single minister to implement emergency legislation), with revised legislation that requires an impact assessment and approval by MPs before legislation comes into effect., The Health Protection (Coronavirus, Restrictions) (England) Regulations 2020 was enacted without an impact assessment, parliamentary approval happened post implementation. There is increasing evidence that lockdowns & other non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) caused harm to large numbers of people.
 
Children's education was harmed, medical treatment delayed & people's health & fitness reduced. Isolation caused mental health issues, especially for children, elderly & those living alone.

Do not restrict charities from providing tents for homeless people, It has been reported that the Government is considering restricting charities from providing tents for homeless people. This cannot be allowed to happen. , Homelessness can be devastating, dangerous and isolating. 

Many of the problems stem from a severe shortage of affordable housing and a lack of appropriate support services & the cost of living crisis. Rough sleeping is up 26% on last year (Kerslake Commission, 2023). If this restriction was to happen, it could leave vulnerable people to face the harsh weather conditions without any shelter whatsoever. Please support this petition so that we can protect the most vulnerable in our society.
