To put in place laws that help homeless people, rather than illegalise them, I am appalled that the government are considering making it illegal for homeless people to live in tents.
This is absolutely disgusting, and does nothing to help the plight that these people are suffering., To debate better means of accomplishing the alleged aim of this legislation. 
That us, to give homelessness more options around what to do when registering as homeless

Fund routine breast cancer screening for people of all ages, The evidence that people under the age of 50 (the current screening age) are being diagnosed with breast cancer is still an issue., People of any age can get breast cancer, so why is screening not offered to anyone that has or is developing breasts?
 
Breast Cancer Now has said that:
 
8 out of 10 cases of breast cancer are diagnosed in women aged 50 and over.
 
1 in 4 of cases are diagnosed in women aged 75 and over.
 
Just over 10,000 women are diagnosed with breast cancer under the age of 50 every year in the UK. Of these, around 7,600 women will be in their 40s.
 
Around 2,400 women in the UK are diagnosed aged 39 or under, or just 4% of all cases.
 
Breast cancer in men is rare with just 400 new cases in the UK each year, compared to around 55,000 new cases in women.

Require local authorities to issue parking permits to health and care workers, Change laws to require local authorities to give carers and healthcare professionals parking permits so we can more easily care for vulnerable people in their own homes. Our vulnerable people still need care., Carers and healthcare professionals help vulnerable people in their own homes. It's important for us to be there for their varying care needs or treatment but parking difficulties can make this vital role difficult at times. A parking permit would help alleviate this issue.

Make it illegal to use a parent parking space without a child, Stop people who don’t have children parking in parent and children spaces., I want the government to make parking in parent and children spaces illegal if you don’t have children. 
 
As trivial as it may seem, this is a real problem for parents with new born or young children.

Review healthcare provision for people moved into temporary accommodation, When homeless people are placed in temporary accommodation it can be out of area. Vulnerable people can then be discharged from their health service, even though the same council is responsible for them. We want the Government to review these arrangements, and how to ensure continuity of healthcare., I am concerned that at present healthcare can be disrupted when a council places a homeless person in temporary accommodation outside of their area. This can have tragic consequences for the individuals involved.

Abolish the High Income Child Benefit Charge, We want the Government to remove the High Income Child Benefit Charge with immediate effect., It's time to rescind what we believe is a flawed and damaging tax on families, and place our children, the future of this country where they belong, at the heart of our society.

Fund breast cancer screening from the age of 40, Currently women are invited for a breast cancer screening mammogram between the age of 50-53. I would like the Government to provide funding to support breast cancer screening being offered from the age of 40., I am a 46 year old mother of 4. In July 2023 I was diagnosed with breast cancer. Due to my type of cancer and the position I never would have been able to feel a lump. My cancer was found by chance, after investigation of something else. The situation worsened when tests showed my cancer had metastasised to my bones. If I had had a routine mammogram at 40 years of age or even 43 I wouldn't now be living with advanced cancer and dying sooner than I should. Many women like myself could be saved.

Require bowel care policies and specialist bowel care at all NHS hospitals, We want the Government to ensure every NHS hospital has a bowel care policy and specialist bowel care. No one should be left unable to go to the toilet, potentially for days, because the hospital doesn’t have a bowel care policy or specialist staff., People with a long-term neurogenic condition that affects the bowel, like spinal cord injury, may need specialised bowel care if in a healthcare setting. We are concerned that not enough NHS trusts in England have a policy on neurogenic bowel dysfunction, or ward-based staff who specialise in looking after someone with a neurogenic bowel condition.

We want the Government to ensure every trust has a policy and specialist staff in place for neurogenic bowel conditions.

Disregard Christmas bonus payments on Universal Credit Claimants, Those who work for an employer and receive a bonus at Christmas time for their hard work and loyalty, should not have their Universal Credit award reduced because of this. We believe any Christmas bonus should be disregarded for the purpose of calculating Universal Credit., Low income workers who are entitled to Universal Credit should not have their Christmas bonuses taken into account on their January Assessment Period. Why should those who have worked hard all year to qualify for a thank you from their employer to ease the cost of Christmas have their Universal Credit reduced in January, when by then it may be long gone? What is the incentive to working? The £10 DWP bonus isn’t taken off Universal Credit claimants in January!

Fund more pet friendly emergency accommodation , I think that the Government should fund more pet friendly emergency accommodation for those who are homeless and have pets., From my own experiences, I know how difficult it can be to keep a pet whilst you're homeless. Homeless people might not have as many friends or family members as other people, so when they have a pet they are very important to them. I also think that opening more accommodation would help with overcrowding at shelters and reduce strain on them.

Make breaking a manifesto pledge trigger a General Election, For any pledge that is part of the published party manifesto, that was in place at the election where the government came to power, if that pledge is subsequently broken, a general election should be triggered., The UK public expect and deserve the highest standards of integrity from its politicians and in recent years manifesto pledges have been broken.
 
Manifesto pledges are one of the main reasons voters choose a particular political party so if the pledges are broken, the voters must be afforded an opportunity to vote again.

Introduce fines for PIP assessment companies if decision is overturned on appeal, Many PIP assessment decisions are overturned either at mandatory reconsideration or at a tribunal. This is a wasteful use of Government resources and causes unnecessary stress for claimants. We want fines to be levied on companies conducting PIP assessments if a decision is overturned on appeal., We believe that in order to enable a correct, fair, and better claimant experience, the assessment companies should be penalised financially when a decision is overturned. This petition calls for the Government to implement this. This could be done by removing the fee paid plus a 50% surcharge from the payments made to the assessment companies. This should help make sure that assessors and companies do the job correctly the first time, and could save the Government money and claimants stress.

Stop car insurers considering age of driver when setting insurance policies, Change the law on considering the age of the driver when setting insurance policies., The law should be changed to make it illegal to increase prices just because of a person's age. We think that if a person is fit to drive, premiums should be of an average cost.
